Note on unblinded specimen s_14844eef0c (bryostatin):

PubChem check (e23) confirms bryostatin CID 6435419, structure/BBBC021 agreement, no curated ChEMBL mechanism; BBBC021 annotation is Kinase inhibitors, which matches the scored MoA. My revised conclusion Kinase inhibitors (p=0.32, e21) was therefore correct by code, after the PI-requested free analysis of the 10 µM well w_63411a268e.

Initial quantitative phenotype: low-mid doses (0.1-0.3 µM) showed strong nuc_dna_mean depression (z -5.2 to -5.0, e4 e7) without actin/tubulin changes, then at 1 µM enlarged spread cells, cell_area z+4.75, pale DAPI, rounder nuclei nuc_eccentricity z-7.6 (e2), with microscopist-reported binucleate giant cell and spiky peripheral actin (e6). High dose 10 µM switched to dominant actin/tubulin texture: act_glcm_contrast z+28.96, tub_glcm_contrast z+10.57, act_std z+16.33 (e3), stellate protrusive morphology (e19). Atlas NSC was split: 2/4 wells Kinase inhibitors, 1/4 Actin disruptors, 1/4 DNA replication; 4/10 neighbours Kinase inhibitors mean similarity 0.64 (e16).

First hypothesis board over-weighted single-well binucleation as Aurora failed cytokinesis (0.48, e17) despite Aurora 0/4 votes 0/10 neighbours and frac_multinucleate_proxy z -1.01 at 1 µM and rho +0.40 p0.6 (e15). The 10 µM microscopist review (e19) requested by PI clarified dose-dependent actin reorganization as the only consistent high-dose feature, with irregular lobed nuclei but decreased nuc_dna_mean arguing against polyploidy, forcing downgrade of Aurora to 0.10 and promotion of Kinase inhibitors to 0.32 (e20).

Literature context: bryostatin is classically described as a PKC modulator acting via PKC/NF-κB dependent mechanisms; e.g. PKC and NF-κB-dependent latency activation (PMID 26199173) and PKC-dependent synaptogenesis effects (PMID 32437156), consistent with BBBC021 Kinase inhibitors grouping. reflection.text:
Unblinding: bryostatin (CID 6435419, name and BBBC021 structure agree e22, e23). No curated ChEMBL mechanisms returned; literature search e24 'bryostatin mechanism PKC kinase inhibitor' 56 hits/5 returned, e25 'bryostatin actin cytoskeleton' 0 hits. Final verdict correct: Kinase inhibitors (agent p=0.32 e21, truth Kinase inhibitors). First submission Aurora kinase inhibitors p=0.48 e18 was not justified and flagged by review.

What got right - eventually:
The low-dose signal was consistently pale/decondensed DNA without cytoskeletal disruption, which fits a kinase effect rather than high-dose toxicity: e4 dose 3 0.1uM nuc_dna_mean z=-5.2, e7 dose 4 0.3uM nuc_dna_mean z=-5.0 with act_glcm_contrast z=-3.0 (no actin change), and e2 dose 5 1uM nuc_dna_mean z=-7.8. The same pale DNA persisted across doses with rho=-0.80 p=0.2 e9, while cell_count rho=-0.80 p=0.2 e14 indicated cytostatic decline rather than strong cytotoxicity. Final atlas over 4 wells e16 correctly captured this ambiguity: NSC Kinase inhibitors 2/4 wells, k-neighbours Kinase inhibitors 4/10, DNA replication 4/10, DNA damage 2/10, Aurora 0/4 and 0/10. The second describe_phenotype e19 at 10uM (actin disruptors, unknown) plus e3 act_glcm_contrast z=+29.0, act_std +16.3 at 10uM showed the high-dose texture spike e11 rho=+0.80 p=0.2 is a distinct high-dose artifact, allowing the revised call to discount it versus the low-mid dose kinase-like phenotype.

What misled and why:
1. Overweighting a single-field visual binucleation. Initial describe_phenotype e6 (2 fields, 8 observations, candidates Aurora) reported enlarged cells/pale round nuclei and one binucleate giant cell at 1uM. I used this plus e2 cell_solidity -5.2, nuc_eccentricity -7.6 and dose trends e13 frac_large_nucleus rho=+0.80 p=0.2 to build Aurora failed cytokinesis in update_hypotheses e17 (0.48). This ignored the quantitative contradiction: frac_multinucleate_proxy at that same 1uM well was z=-1.01 per review, and across doses rho=+0.40 p=0.6 e15 - no clean multinucleation, peak cell/nuclear area only at that dose and falling by 10uM.
2. Selective dose interpretation. Pale DNA is already maximal at 0.1-0.3uM e4/e7 where actin is normal, which generic Kinase/DNA-replication effects explain equally well. I treated it as Aurora-specific decondensation/polyploidy.
3. Ignoring atlas prior. First compare_to_reference_atlas e5 was already split (Kinase 2/3, Actin 3/10, Eg5 3/10), final e16 gave Aurora zero votes. Assigning 0.48 to Aurora was over-concentrated versus the runner-ups as critique noted.
4. Acquisition choice: I sampled only 4 wells (1uM, 10uM, 0.1uM, then 0.3uM e2-e4-e7) and ran dose_response over n=4 doses with all p=0.2-0.6 e8-e15. I then treated non-significant trends as supporting Aurora, and did not acquire a visual phenotype at the informative high-dose well until forced. Review-requested e19 on w_63411a268e 10uM (already acquired quantitatively in e3) was decisive - it showed dominant actin fragmentation with only inconsistent multinucleation, collapsing the Aurora case.

What was missed / what literature adds:
Lookup showed no curated mechanism, so atlas was the only prior. Literature found in this run supports bryostatin as PKC-dependent kinase modulator, not a primary actin disruptor or selective Aurora inhibitor: PMID 26199173 reports bryostatin activates latent expression through a PKC and NF-kB-dependent mechanism, PMID 32437156 reports bryostatin 1 promotes synaptogenesis through a PKC-Dependent Mechanism, PMID 9738012 and PMID 10197446 describe PKCalpha and PKD phosphorylation-dependent activation contexts. This aligns with the final broad Kinase inhibitors label; e24 hit and e25 zero hits predicted the actin texture as secondary. Specificity to kinase subfamily cannot be resolved from this imaging alone.

Lessons: Do not elevate a single well/single cell phenotype (e6 2 fields) over atlas votes and quantitative multinucleation metrics; require significant dose_response and replicate visual scoring at both mid and high doses before invoking polyploidy; keep hypothesis probability dispersed when e16 neighbours are split 4/10 vs 4/10.

This reflection concerns cell-biology screening data only and does not constitute clinical advice.

## Reflection

Unblinding: bryostatin (CID 6435419, name and BBBC021 structure agree e22, e23). No curated ChEMBL mechanisms returned; literature search e24 'bryostatin mechanism PKC kinase inhibitor' 56 hits/5 returned, e25 'bryostatin actin cytoskeleton' 0 hits. Final verdict correct: Kinase inhibitors (agent p=0.32 e21, truth Kinase inhibitors). First submission Aurora kinase inhibitors p=0.48 e18 was not justified and flagged by review.

What got right - eventually:
The low-dose signal was consistently pale/decondensed DNA without cytoskeletal disruption, which fits a kinase effect rather than high-dose toxicity: e4 dose 3 0.1uM nuc_dna_mean z=-5.2, e7 dose 4 0.3uM nuc_dna_mean z=-5.0 with act_glcm_contrast z=-3.0 (no actin change), and e2 dose 5 1uM nuc_dna_mean z=-7.8. The same pale DNA persisted across doses with rho=-0.80 p=0.2 e9, while cell_count rho=-0.80 p=0.2 e14 indicated cytostatic decline rather than strong cytotoxicity. Final atlas over 4 wells e16 correctly captured this ambiguity: NSC Kinase inhibitors 2/4 wells, k-neighbours Kinase inhibitors 4/10, DNA replication 4/10, DNA damage 2/10, Aurora 0/4 and 0/10. The second describe_phenotype e19 at 10uM (actin disruptors, unknown) plus e3 act_glcm_contrast z=+29.0, act_std +16.3 at 10uM showed the high-dose texture spike e11 rho=+0.80 p=0.2 is a distinct high-dose artifact, allowing the revised call to discount it versus the low-mid dose kinase-like phenotype.

What misled and why:
1. Overweighting a single-field visual binucleation. Initial describe_phenotype e6 (2 fields, 8 observations, candidates Aurora) reported enlarged cells/pale round nuclei and one binucleate giant cell at 1uM. I used this plus e2 cell_solidity -5.2, nuc_eccentricity -7.6 and dose trends e13 frac_large_nucleus rho=+0.80 p=0.2 to build Aurora failed cytokinesis in update_hypotheses e17 (0.48). This ignored the quantitative contradiction: frac_multinucleate_proxy at that same 1uM well was z=-1.01 per review, and across doses rho=+0.40 p=0.6 e15 - no clean multinucleation, peak cell/nuclear area only at that dose and falling by 10uM.
2. Selective dose interpretation. Pale DNA is already maximal at 0.1-0.3uM e4/e7 where actin is normal, which generic Kinase/DNA-replication effects explain equally well. I treated it as Aurora-specific decondensation/polyploidy.
3. Ignoring atlas prior. First compare_to_reference_atlas e5 was already split (Kinase 2/3, Actin 3/10, Eg5 3/10), final e16 gave Aurora zero votes. Assigning 0.48 to Aurora was over-concentrated versus the runner-ups as critique noted.
4. Acquisition choice: I sampled only 4 wells (1uM, 10uM, 0.1uM, then 0.3uM e2-e4-e7) and ran dose_response over n=4 doses with all p=0.2-0.6 e8-e15. I then treated non-significant trends as supporting Aurora, and did not acquire a visual phenotype at the informative high-dose well until forced. Review-requested e19 on w_63411a268e 10uM (already acquired quantitatively in e3) was decisive - it showed dominant actin fragmentation with only inconsistent multinucleation, collapsing the Aurora case.

What was missed / what literature adds:
Lookup showed no curated mechanism, so atlas was the only prior. Literature found in this run supports bryostatin as PKC-dependent kinase modulator, not a primary actin disruptor or selective Aurora inhibitor: PMID 26199173 reports bryostatin activates latent expression through a PKC and NF-kB-dependent mechanism, PMID 32437156 reports bryostatin 1 promotes synaptogenesis through a PKC-Dependent Mechanism, PMID 9738012 and PMID 10197446 describe PKCalpha and PKD phosphorylation-dependent activation contexts. This aligns with the final broad Kinase inhibitors label; e24 hit and e25 zero hits predicted the actin texture as secondary. Specificity to kinase subfamily cannot be resolved from this imaging alone.

Lessons: Do not elevate a single well/single cell phenotype (e6 2 fields) over atlas votes and quantitative multinucleation metrics; require significant dose_response and replicate visual scoring at both mid and high doses before invoking polyploidy; keep hypothesis probability dispersed when e16 neighbours are split 4/10 vs 4/10.
